assessments.reasoning: In the reopened retained Fifth Edition, §2.10 requires processors to deliver non-markup characters to the application and gives validating processors an additional duty to identify whitespace in element content. Section 4.4.2 treats included replacement text as document input at the reference site, where its markup is recognized normally. The delivery rule therefore reaches its character data in content. Section 2.11 sets the input-normalization boundary. Sections 4.4.3 and 5.1 establish when external material must be read and delimit the declaration-processing duties of non-validating processors.

challenge.method: Apply the rule to an included entity containing both text and tags, a literal CRLF in an external parsed entity, and a recognized external parsed entity left unread during non-validating processing.
challenge.results: Included text reaches the application while the tags are parsed as markup. A literal CRLF yields one line feed before parsing. Permitted omission under §4.4.3 requires notice that the entity was recognized and left unread. Validation requires processing the entire DTD and the referenced external parsed entities. Each case fits the claim's restriction to processed character data during normal processing.

limitations: Under §4.4.3, an XML processor that is not validating may omit replacement text for a recognized external parsed entity reference covered by that clause. If it omits the replacement text, it must notify the application that the entity was recognized and unread.

Under §5.1, validating processors read and process the entire DTD and referenced external parsed entities. The source separately specifies the obligatory processing of declarations read by non-validating processors.
Section 2.11 normalizes literal line endings before parsing. Section 2.10 also requires validating processors to identify white space in element content.

The finding covers XML 1.0 Fifth Edition normal processing and the non-markup character data in document content after applicable input normalization, including entity replacement text that is included.
This is a specification reading. It establishes no particular parser API, callback granularity, processor conformance result, or downstream application handling.
